{{Short description|German mathematician (1924–1990)}}

[[File:Max Koecher 2.jpeg|thumb|right|Max Koecher in Munich, 1967]]
'''Max Koecher''' ({{IPA|de|ˈkœçɐ|lang}}; 20 January 1924 in [[Weimar]] – 7 February 1990, [[Lengerich (Westfalen)|Lengerich]]) was a German mathematician.

==Biography==
Koecher studied mathematics and physics at the [[University of Göttingen]].
In 1951, he received his doctorate under [[Max Deuring]] with his work {{harv|Koecher|1953}} on Dirichlet series with functional equation where he introduced [[Koecher–Maass series]]. He qualified in 1954 at the [[University of Münster]]. From 1962 to 1970, Koecher was department chair at [[LMU Munich]]. He retired in 1989.

His main research area was the theory of Jordan algebras, where he introduced the [[Kantor–Koecher–Tits construction]] and the [[Koecher–Vinberg theorem]], and introduced the concept of an [[admissible algebra]].  He discovered the  [[Koecher boundedness principle]] in the theory of [[Siegel modular form]]s
